title: Worlds 2026: Waters Wins Her 46th Triple Crown as 15-Year-Old Shimabukuro Becomes the Youngest Men's Doubles Champion in PPA History
excerpt: Anna Leigh Waters swept all three titles at the Opendoor Pickleball World Championships in Farmers Branch, Texas, while 15-year-old Tama Shimabukuro and JW Johnson rallied from two games down to win the men's doubles crown.
content:
The biggest week in professional pickleball ended Sunday, Nov. 8, at Brookhaven Country Club in Farmers Branch, Texas, with Anna Leigh Waters once again standing at the center of it — and a 15-year-old stealing a share of the spotlight.

Waters won her 46th career Triple Crown at the Opendoor Pickleball World Championships, sweeping all three events she entered. In women's singles, the top seed beat No. 2 Kate Fahey 11-3, 11-2. In mixed doubles, Waters and Ben Johns outlasted Jorja Johnson and JW Johnson 9-11, 11-6, 11-9, 3-11, 11-4. And in women's doubles, Waters and Anna Bright beat Catherine Parenteau and Sofia Sewing 11-4, 11-9, 11-5 for their record 18th consecutive title together.

The men's doubles final produced the week's biggest story. JW Johnson and 15-year-old Tama Shimabukuro dropped the first two games to Christian Alshon and Andrei Daescu, then stormed back to win 5-11, 5-11, 11-4, 11-8, 11-4. Shimabukuro is the youngest men's doubles champion in PPA Tour history.

In men's singles, No. 7 seed John Lucian Goins beat No. 13 Jack Sock 11-5, 12-10 for the title. The World Championships, a PPA Major, paid out about $1.65 million across the week.

The week opened with team play. The United States swept Latin America 3-0 in the final of the first MLP Nations Cup on Nov. 1 at the same venue, winning the women's game 11-9, the men's game 11-1 and the mixed game 11-6 to finish the event unbeaten at 5-0.

While the pros played in Texas, the amateur game had its own championship week. The 2026 USA Pickleball National Championships wrapped up in San Diego after nine days at Barnes Tennis Center, drawing nearly 2,300 players. Jack Munro and Richard Livornese defended their men's doubles title, and Livornese added a second gold in mixed doubles with Kat Stewart.

The week also set up next season. Eight players earned 2027 PPA Tour contracts at the Challenger Showdown, played alongside Worlds in Farmers Branch. Eileen Wang and Matt Burkhardt won the singles titles to lead the group turning pro full time next year.

Sources: PPA Tour (ppatour.com), Nov. 8, 2026; World Pickleball Magazine, Nov. 2, 2026; ThePickleHub, Nov. 2, 2026; Forbes / The Kitchen / The Dink, Nov. 10-12, 2026.
